labels.text: Usage: /workflow <goal>. Plans the goal into stages and runs each step as a subagent.

S62.01.needs: a session where subagents can start (a model run that can call the task tool)
S62.01.note: The list belongs to the session. Parent ownership is implied, not labelled; the Code line's registry.rs:484 is the /tasks list function.
steps: Start agi and send a request that makes the model spawn subagents, for example /workflow <goal>.
When subagents have started, type /tasks and press Enter.
Look for the line "Subagent tasks (N)" and the rows under it.
Compare with Expected: the rows are the child tasks of this session. No line on screen names a parent task.

S62.02.needs: a session with at least one subagent
steps: Start a run with at least one subagent, for example /workflow <goal>.
Type /tasks and press Enter.
Look for "Subagent tasks (N)" with one row per child: id, role, status and description.
Compare with Expected: each child working under the task appears as a row.

S62.03.needs: a session with at least one subagent
S62.03.note: The role column has no heading in the list output.
steps: Run /tasks and read the second column of each row, for example reviewer or general-purpose.
Type /tasks show <id> with a row id from the list.
Look for the header "Task <id> [status] role: description".
Compare with Expected: each child shows its role label. The list has no column heading for role.

S62.04.note: The Model line appears only after the task has a result; a running or failed task with no usage shows no model.
steps: Run /tasks and copy the id of a finished subagent.
Type /tasks show <id> and press Enter.
Look for the line starting with "Model" that gives the model name, tokens and cost.
Compare with Expected: the model name labels that agent. The list view does not show the model.

S62.05.needs: a session where two or more subagents run at the same time
S62.05.note: /tasks prints a snapshot into the chat; it does not refresh. The live cue shows only a count, not per-agent status.
steps: Start a run that spawns subagents and, while they are still working, type /tasks.
Read the [running] status on each row.
Wait, then type /tasks again and read the status change, for example [completed] or [failed: ...].
Compare with Expected: each agent has its own status. Also watch the working line above the prompt for the count of subagents working at once.
Run /tasks and copy the id of a finished subagent.
Type /tasks show <id> and press Enter.
Read the block under the header: it holds that task's result text, then Files modified if any.
Repeat for a second id and compare with Expected: each agent's result is its own block.

S62.08.note: Usage appears only after the agent finishes.
steps: Run /tasks show <id> for a finished subagent.
Read the Model line: input and output tokens, then the cost in credits or "on your subscription".
Run the same for a second finished subagent.
Compare with Expected: usage is shown per agent. No session total per agent appears in this view.

S62.09.needs: two or more subagents running at the same time
S62.09.note: Searched apps/cli/src for a live multi-task panel. Found only the /tasks text list (a snapshot) and the working-line count "working at once" in tui_app.rs. No single live overview of several running tasks was found.

S62.11.needs: a subagent that asks for a permission
S62.11.note: The approval box floats over the chat, not an overview. The overlay code has no subagent-specific label, so the box may not show which agent is asking.
steps: Start a run where a subagent needs permission, for example /workflow <goal> that edits files, in a permission mode that asks.
When the "Tool Approval" box appears over the chat, read its key list.
Press the key that approves the request.
Type /tasks and check the waiting task now shows [running] or a later status. Compare with Expected: unblocked without leaving the view.
S62.11.where: Any request that needs approval > "Tool Approval" box

S62.12.needs: a finished subagent that kept a transcript
S62.12.note: If the task kept no transcript the app says so. The drill-down is a typed command, not a click.
steps: Run /tasks and copy the id of a finished subagent.
Type /tasks show <id> and read the last line, which gives the step count and the command.
Type /tasks transcript <id> and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the full conversation of that task appears, step by step.

S62.16.needs: a request that takes a while to answer
S62.16.note: The code cited tui_app.rs:7304 is an input-handling line, not a fork. /btw is the closest match. /background (/bg) hands the whole conversation to a background run and clears the chat, so it does not match.
steps: Send a long request to the main chat so it keeps working.
While it is working, type /btw <question>, for example /btw what is the project name, and press Enter.
Read the status "answering the side question" and the side answer in the chat.
Compare with Expected: the side question is answered while the main request keeps running.

S62.17.needs: a conversation with messages and session saving on (not --no-session-persistence)
S62.17.note: The branch is created as a separate managed session. It is not opened interactively in the current screen.
steps: Send a few messages so the conversation has content.
Type /fork and press Enter.
Read the reply "Branched conversation '<name>' as managed session <id>. Resume with: agiworkforce --session <id>".
Compare with Expected: the branch is not continued on the same screen; resume it with the printed command in a new run.

labels.text: Usage: /advisor <question>, consult a catalog-selected advisor model

S62.18.needs: an advisor model available in the catalog
S62.18.note: The agent can also call the advisor tool itself; that path is not a typed step.
steps: Type /advisor followed by a question, for example /advisor is this plan safe to ship?, and press Enter.
Wait for the advisor reply in the chat.
Read the end of the reply, which shows the line "[advisor model: <name>]".
Compare with Expected: the answer from the advisor model is shown. If it fails, the chat shows "Advisor failed:".
